message.reasoning_content: We need to determine crimes based on facts. The facts: LiXX had severe disease, wanted revenge. On Sep 29 2014, he opened gas stove, intended to cause gas explosion by dialing phone to create spark. Neighbour discovered, called police, gas shut, no explosion. Next day, he went with a knife to a commercial area, stabbed 20 people, causing various injuries: some heavy, some light, some minor. So crimes: attempted arson? Actually causing gas explosion is dangerous. The act of opening gas stove and attempting to cause explosion is "放火" (arson) or "非法制造、买卖、运输、邮寄、储存、使用危险物质罪"? In Chinese criminal law, causing explosion by gas is "放火罪" (arson) if it endangers public safety. Since no explosion occurred, maybe "未遂放火罪" (attempted arson). Also "故意伤害罪" for stabbing many people. Possibly "故意伤害致重伤罪" for those with heavy injuries, and "故意伤害致轻伤罪" for light injuries. In examples, they sometimes combine multiple injuries into one label: e.g., "故意伤害;编造、故意传播虚假恐怖信息". So we can list "故意伤害" as generic. Also "放火" for attempted arson. Could also be "危害公共安全罪" (endangering public safety) but examples use "放火". So answer: [罪名]放火;故意伤害<eoa>
